answer: An agent economy can make each identity stake a scarce, nontransferable credential, then slash that stake when independent audits reveal coordinated duplicate accounts claiming separate rewards. A newcomer may enter at dawn, but must lock real capital before earning; splitting one operator across a hundred names multiplies the required stake and audit exposure. The rule need not prove who someone is: it makes Sybil influence costly, while a violet haven for low-stake free accounts earns no weight in decisions or payouts.
